verdictBasis: 0 blockers, 1 SHOULD-FIX, 2 advisories. The dispatch gate is ACCEPT only at 0 blockers AND 0 SHOULD-FIX, so ACCEPT is not available. The carry discipline is excellent — the 23-line file-03 block, the file-02 developer-contract line, and the DR-108 register row all reproduce byte-exact against live sources at the pinned digests, and every authority denial the row demands is present and honest. The single SHOULD-FIX is that one of the three broker prohibitions is a normative obligation with no provenance in any source this artifact pins, and its presence falsifies the artifact's own authorityClaim enumeration.

shouldFix.title: proposedBroker.mustNot[2] is an unsourced component-containment obligation, and it makes authorityClaim's three-item enumeration false as written
shouldFix.what: mustNot[2] reads 'let a component store or retrieve credentials outside the host broker'. Its two siblings both trace to text this artifact carries: mustNot[0] ('log the secret value') comes from the carried sentence 'A future broker may resolve an admitted secret handle for one bound operation without logging the value', and mustNot[1] ('emit the value into PlanId, evidence digest, diagnostics, or support bundles') comes from the carried V1 law 'the value is excluded from PlanId, evidence digest, diagnostics, and support bundles'. mustNot[2] traces to neither. I diffed the entire carried block (file 03 lines 41-63, byte-exact, verified) and it contains no component-containment rule of any kind; its only broker sentence is the one the artifact already quotes at proposedBroker.may.
shouldFix.whyThisIsAFinding: Three independent reasons, each checkable on pinned bytes. (1) NO PROVENANCE. This artifact is otherwise rigorous about provenance — it carries 23 file-03 lines verbatim under a digest, pins file 02 at exactly line 184 under a digest, and quotes the DR-108 row verbatim under a digest and line number. mustNot[2] is stated with no source at all, inside an object whose sibling key `may` is a verbatim quotation, so a reader reasonably reads the whole object as carried. (2) THE AUTHORITY CLAIM UNDER-DESCRIBES THE ARTIFACT. authorityClaim enumerates exactly three proposals — 'the preserved V1 secret-value/handle scope, the proposed (not inherited) keychain plus verified-permission user-file fallback, and the one-bound-operation broker remainder'. A prohibition on where components may store or retrieve credentials is a fourth element outside all three, so the enumeration is false as written: the artifact does more than it says it does. That is the corpus bar for SHOULD-FIX, and it is met without needing to settle any question about containment philosophy. (3) IT CROSSES INTO NEIGHBOURING ROWS UNCAVEATED. The nearest live support is file 02 line 191 — components 'must not ... bypass host brokers' — which this artifact neither carries, pins, nor cites, even though it already pins file 02 for line 184. Meanwhile file 03 assigns the broker-grant machinery to a different row ('This is a proposed V2 mechanism at DR-105, not evidence that any current platform enforces it') and its confinement-honesty section states 'Host brokers used voluntarily by an unconstrained same-user process do not create confinement.' A flat mustNot, stated without that caveat, reads as a containment property that the pinned source expressly declines to promise. The artifact routes DR-125 for SDK APIs, so the failure to route this one is an asymmetry in its own discipline, not an oversight the reader can be expected to supply.
shouldFix.consequence: If recorded as-is, a later decision could cite this artifact as having extracted 'components may not store or retrieve credentials outside the host broker' from file 03, when file 03 says no such thing at DR-108. That is precisely the attribution error this corpus has graded before — a wider rule attributed to an accepted narrower document.
shouldFix.notOverstated: I am not claiming the obligation is wrong or undesirable. file 02 line 191 makes it plausible V2 policy. The finding is about provenance and self-description, both of which are repairable without changing the artifact's position.
shouldFix.suggestedFix: Either (a) drop mustNot[2] and let DR-105 own component-broker containment, or (b) keep it and make it honest: add file 02 line 191 to the carry with its line number under the digest already pinned at sdkHandleCarry, mark the item as reaching beyond the DR-108 file-03 carry, attach file 03's 'voluntary host brokers do not create confinement' caveat, route the enforcement question to DR-105 / DR-117 the way sdkHandleCarry already routes DR-125, and extend authorityClaim so its enumeration covers what the artifact actually proposes.

advisories.title: The carried block contains a live cross-artifact freeze claim that the artifact neither extracts nor routes
advisories.detail: The carry faithfully includes the CFG-6 paragraph: RESOLVED-INPUTS v2 holds a stale CFG-6 note about TM v2; pinned TM v3 restores finding V11 and records A1-TM2-01 resolved; 'TM remains UNSET — BLOCKS FREEZE for V10/custody/G19, not for CFG-6'; and the stale note is a DR-011 reconciliation residual. The artifact extracts none of it and routes none of it, while the DR-108 row's acceptance-evidence cell names a 'Platform threat model' and evidenceRemainder marks that NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED. A reader is left to work out unaided whether the TM freeze-block bears on DR-108's threat-model remainder.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: Carrying more context than one extracts is the conservative choice and the carry is byte-exact, so nothing is misrepresented. The artifact states these sentences in the source's voice, not its own, and makes no claim about the TM's standing. On the merits the two are distinguishable — the carried text scopes the freeze-block to V10/custody/G19 and expressly not to CFG-6, whereas DR-108 needs a platform threat model — so the silence hides no contradiction.
advisories.suggestedFix: One clause noting that the carried CFG-6/TM sentences are DR-011/TM territory carried for completeness, and that DR-108's 'Platform threat model' remainder is distinct from the TM freeze-block scoped to V10/custody/G19.

coordinatorNote: This is a good artifact with one repairable seam. Its carry discipline is the strongest part and it holds under exact measurement: 23 file-03 lines byte-identical and cleanly bounded, the file-02 developer-contract line exact, the DR-108 row exact and located by ID at the line it claims, and all four source digests reproducing at a COORD pin measured at the live HEAD rather than inherited. It keeps the passages that hurt it — the source-embedded-credentials disclaimer and the TM freeze paragraph — which is the behaviour of an artifact trying to be checked rather than believed. It also anticipates its own most dangerous sentence: the slice-irrelevance claim is exactly what a D-096 (A) deferral would masquerade as, and it is guarded explicitly and is independently true, since D-002 itself names DR-108 as having no credential-requiring features in slice 1. What blocks ACCEPT is narrow. Two of the three broker prohibitions trace to carried text; the third, forbidding components to store or retrieve credentials outside the host broker, traces to nothing this artifact pins. Its nearest support is file 02 line 191, which the artifact does not carry even though it already pins that file for line 184; the mechanism it leans on is assigned by file 03 to DR-105; and file 03's confinement-honesty section expressly denies that voluntary host-broker use creates confinement, a caveat the flat prohibition omits. The cleanest way to see it is that authorityClaim enumerates three proposals and the artifact makes four, so its self-description is false as written. That is repairable in a v2 without moving the artifact's position at all — either drop the item to DR-105, or carry and caveat it properly and widen the enumeration to match. 0 blockers, 1 SHOULD-FIX, 2 advisories: REJECT.
